en: Dependent on a cause that is with refuge (*saraṇa*), a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor with refuge arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor with refuge, a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor with refuge arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on both a phenomenon that is a cause with refuge and a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor with refuge, a phenomenon that is neither a cause nor with refuge arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition (hetu), there are three; with respect to the predominance condition (adhipati), there are three ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition (avigata), there are three.
In dependence on a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict (nahetu-araṇa), a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict arises by way of the root condition.

In dependence on a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict as condition, a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict arises by way of the root condition. [In dependence on] a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict ...
Conditioned by a state that is neither-root nor-obstruction, states that are neither-root nor-obstruction arise by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition] there are three.
